speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2013-2014, seeking just over $4.8 billion in appropriations including about $1.3 billion in equity for NBN Co to continue the broadband rollout, $683 million for Defence equipment purchases under the 2013 Defence White Paper, and $604 million for AusAID's contribution to the World Bank's International Development Association.

speeches.speaker: Warren Truss
speeches.brief: Accused the government of falsely claiming a $100 billion infrastructure centrepiece when the budget actually cuts road and rail funding from $36 billion to $24 billion, said mining tax revenue has collapsed from a forecast $22.5 billion to just $3 billion, 95 per cent below estimate, and noted the $3 billion Melbourne Metro project has only $75 million allocated in the forward estimates.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Criticised the budget as full of unfunded visions, including a very fast train that could take 40 years and cost $120 billion, and a promised $405 million to bring forward the M2 to F3 missing link in Sydney meant to take 700 trucks and 75,000 cars a day off Pennant Hills Road, which he found was not actually funded until 2015-16 at the earliest.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Contrasted the coalition's last $19.7 billion surplus with Labor's $19.4 billion deficit this year, said Australia entered the global financial crisis with a $20 billion surplus and $60 billion in the Future Fund, and noted the Treasurer's promised $1.5 billion surplus became a deficit more than 12 times as large.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Defended the budget, saying DisabilityCare will launch in 34 days and cover more than 2,000 people with disability in his Moreton electorate, highlighted the increase in the superannuation guarantee from nine to 12 per cent boosting retirement savings for 8.4 million Australians, and noted Australia holds a AAA credit rating, one of only eight countries to do so.

speeches.speaker: Russell Broadbent
speeches.brief: Noted that his Gippsland-based McMillan electorate produces 24 per cent of the nation's milk and nearly 90 per cent of Victoria's power, accused the government of gutting the Latrobe Valley transition fund to just $15 million over six years despite an earlier $200 million Contract for Closure commitment, and criticised weekend penalty rates that can see a teenager paid $29 an hour to wash dishes.

speeches.speaker: Geoff Lyons
speeches.brief: Reported that around 1,850 people in his Bass electorate will be eligible for DisabilityCare, noted more than 6,900 local families with 12,100 schoolchildren benefit from the Schoolkids Bonus, and warned that if the coalition's Joe Hockey became Treasurer he could redirect the GST formula in a way that puts $600 million of Tasmania's revenue at risk.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Retorted that without Labor there would be no NDIS at all, and noted the opposition's willingness to accept this year's budget undercuts its own criticism of it.

speeches.speaker: Rob Mitchell
speeches.brief: Defended the government's budget, citing Australia's AAA credit rating from all three ratings agencies, held by only eight countries worldwide, said lower interest rates leave a typical mortgage holder more than $100 a week better off than under the previous government, and accused the opposition of planning to raise the GST by at least 2.5 per cent and impose a 1.6 per cent tax increase on businesses to fund its paid parental leave scheme.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: Criticised the budget as chaotic and directionless, welcoming a $4.5 million saving from scrapping the internet filter as its one redeeming feature, warned gross debt would breach the $300 billion ceiling for the first time, and said defence spending as a share of GDP had fallen to its lowest level since 1938 after a further $25 million cut.

speeches.speaker: Ken O'Dowd
speeches.brief: Warned Australia was at an economic crossroads, citing $100 billion worth of resource projects shelved or scrapped due to sovereign risk and costs, said the $300 billion gross debt is costing $20 million a day in interest, and criticised the National Broadband Network rollout in his electorate of Flynn as so slow it would take 100 years to complete at the current rate.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Argued that the appropriations bills were standard supply measures underpinning the 2013-14 budget, said the coalition would not oppose them, and criticised the government's fiscal management by citing receipts of $350 billion, expenditure of $367 billion and projected gross debt closer to $400 billion than $300 billion.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Criticised the budget for a $19.4 billion deficit and projected gross debt of $370 billion by 2016-17, said his Grey electorate covers more than 90 per cent of South Australia's land mass and its resources, including major aquaculture around Port Lincoln, and called for the government to consolidate six rival proposals for a deep-sea port within 200 kilometres of each other on the Spencer Gulf.

speeches.speaker: Ewen Jones
speeches.brief: Criticised the government for the loss of 200,000 small business jobs since 2007, with small business's share of the workforce falling from 54.7 per cent to 46 per cent, called for fair indexation of Defence Force retirement benefits unfairly excluded since 1972, and said the budget delivers a $325 million cut to education despite Gonski promises.

speeches.speaker: Tony Crook
speeches.brief: Welcomed $400,000 in Regional Development Australia funding for the Esperance foreshore redevelopment, contrasting it with the $17 million the same shire previously received under Western Australia's Royalties for Regions program, and warned that Western Australia's GST return could fall to just 42 per cent even as almost $15 billion more in taxes leaves the state for the Commonwealth each year.

speeches.speaker: Bruce Scott
speeches.brief: Blamed the 2011 live cattle export ban to Indonesia for a $46.5 million quarterly loss at the Australian Agricultural Company and cattle prices falling by up to 50 per cent, with some Longreach cattle selling for just $20 a head, and called for $8 million to build an 800-kilometre dingo barrier fence to protect the region's declining sheep industry.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Criticised the budget for rising debt, repeated deficits, higher taxes and broken promises, cited concerns from business organisations about small-business conditions, and outlined coalition proposals including abolishing the carbon and mining taxes and reducing regulation.

speeches.speaker: Barry Haase
speeches.brief: Criticised Labor's budget management, arguing that the government had replaced a strong fiscal position with deficits, debt and broken promises, including a projected deficit of $19.4 billion instead of the promised surplus.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Challenged the budget's fiscal record, noting the debt ceiling has been raised four times from $75 billion to $300 billion, said the government's NBN Co investment has been slashed by $3.5 billion over three years, and cited a $4.7 billion cost blow-out in border protection since more than 42,000 people arrived on 694 boats.

speeches.speaker: Jill Hall
speeches.brief: Defended the budget as responsible, citing Australia's AAA credit rating from every ratings agency, the government's $9.8 billion investment in new school funding including New South Wales Premier O'Farrell's agreement to sign on, and the NDIS trial beginning in the Hunter region benefiting people with disability in her electorate.

speeches.speaker: Bert Van Manen
speeches.brief: Argued residents in his Forde electorate, including small businesses, pensioners and young families, are struggling under the government's cost-of-living pressures and new taxes, quoting the Leader of the Opposition's description of a great country let down by a bad government.

speeches.speaker: Paul Neville
speeches.brief: Criticised the budget's credibility, noting the mining tax was originally predicted to raise $22.5 billion but has fallen to just $3.3 billion over four years, said the carbon price forecast has been cut from $38 a tonne to $12 a tonne at a cost of $5 billion in revenue, and pointed to a $10 billion blowout from asylum seeker boat arrivals.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: Highlighted that Victoria has more than 172 railway level crossings compared with just eight in Sydney, with no federal funding for the worst in her Higgins electorate, said electricity prices have risen 93.8 per cent since 2007, and said the budget cuts school funding by more than $325 million despite Gonski rhetoric.

speeches.speaker: Karen Andrews
speeches.brief: Criticised the government for promising a $1.5 billion surplus but delivering a $19.4 billion deficit, a $20.9 billion turnaround worth more than 20 times the funding once allocated to upgrade the M1 in her electorate, and said interest on government debt now costs $35 million a day amid a 90 per cent rise in electricity prices and a 64 per cent rise in gas prices since 2007.
